readerTitle: Why some marketing keeps working after you stop paying
caseNote: 가상 사례 (원예용품점, 창고용 선반 제조사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 마케팅 지출은 돈을 내는 동안만 효과가 있는 '임대'와, 한 번 만들면 계속 고객을 데려오는 '자산'으로 나뉜다. 유용한 콘텐츠와 커뮤니티는 자산 쪽이다.
misconception: 콘텐츠와 커뮤니티는 광고처럼 바로 효과를 내는 공짜 마케팅이다. 또는 효과가 바로 안 보이니 쓸모없다.

sources.text: 마케팅의 일반 개념 (유료 매체 vs 소유 매체, 콘텐츠·커뮤니티의 누적 효과)

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 1년 차 광고 $3,000 + 가이드 $3,000 = $6,000 예산과 일치합니다. 차트: 광고 신규 고객 120 / 0 / 0, 가이드 신규 고객 30 / 90 / 110 (2~3년 차에는 새 지출 없음). 3년 합계는 광고 120명, 가이드 230명입니다.
2~3년 차에 가이드 유입이 늘어난다는 가정은 검색 노출과 공유가 쌓인다는 설명용 가정입니다. 실제로는 업종과 콘텐츠 품질에 따라 크게 다릅니다. 카드에 illustrative 표시가 있습니다.

cards.title: The ad stopped. The tomato guide didn't.
body: One spring, a garden center ran search ads. It also wrote a short online guide: *Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow?*
When the ad budget ran out, the ad customers stopped that same week. Three springs later, people still walk in holding that guide on their phones.

image.label: Customer at a garden center showing a tomato guide on her phone
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 동네 원예용품점 계산대 앞에서 손님이 휴대폰 화면(노란 잎 토마토 그림이 있는 가이드 페이지)을 점원에게 보여줌. 배경 한쪽에 꺼진 광고 전광판. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your $6,000 marketing budget
body: You run a garden center with $6,000 for marketing this year. Search ads bring customers right away. Writing seasonal growing guides and hosting a monthly plant-swap group takes months to show results.
How do you split the money?

options.text: All $6,000 on ads. They work now.
options.feedback: You get customers fast and can count them. But once the money is spent, nothing keeps working for you next year.

options.text: All $6,000 on guides and the plant-swap group
options.feedback: You might build something lasting, but this year's sales lose their main source while you wait. A slow asset can't pay this month's rent.

options.text: Most on ads for now, plus a steady share on guides and the group every month
options.feedback: Ads carry this year's sales while you build something that grows. Over time, you may need less ad spending to get the same customers.

cards.title: Where her new customers came from
body: In year one she spent $3,000 on ads and $3,000 on guides. After that, she spent nothing new on either.
cards.callout: The ads won year one. The guides kept going.

cards.title: Content and community as assets
body: An **asset** is something you pay for once that keeps producing value. A delivery van is an asset. So is a useful guide that keeps bringing in customers.

Paid ads work more like rent: you get the space only while you pay. **Content** (guides, videos, how-tos) and **community** (customers who meet, share and help each other) are things you own and can keep adding to.

image.label: Two paths: a rented billboard versus a growing stack of guides
image.brief: 좌우 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽: 동전을 넣는 동안만 불이 켜지는 광고판("Rent"). 오른쪽: 해마다 한 권씩 쌓이는 가이드 책 더미와 그 옆에 모인 사람들("Own"). 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Why assets pile up
body: Each new piece adds to a stock instead of replacing the last one.
list: **Old pieces keep working:** last year's guide still answers this year's question
**They stack:** ten guides answer more questions than one
**Community spreads itself:** members help each other and bring friends
**You hold the relationship:** an email list or local group doesn't vanish when a budget ends
cards.callout: Ads add customers. Assets raise the *rate* at which customers keep arriving.
cards.softwareNote: Many software companies run help guides and user forums. Users answer each other's questions, which lowers support costs, and those public answers bring in new users through search.

cards.title: Assets wear down and need upkeep.
body: Content goes stale. A guide with outdated advice can hurt trust, and a community without a host goes quiet. Most assets also take months before they bring meaningful customers.
If your audience lives only on a social platform, you're still partly renting. One rule change can cut your reach overnight.
And it only works if it's genuinely useful. A sales pitch dressed up as a guide builds nothing.

cards.title: Now it's a shelving manufacturer.
body: You make steel shelving and racking for warehouses. Engineers and warehouse managers keep emailing your sales team the same questions: How much weight can this shelf hold? How far apart should the uprights be?
Where do you put next year's extra marketing effort?

options.text: Run more ads in trade magazines
options.feedback: Ads reach new buyers this quarter, but every buyer they bring still emails the same questions. Nothing builds up.

options.text: Publish clear load guides and a simple planning tool on your site, and share them with customers
options.feedback: Each guide answers a question once for every future buyer, and engineers who find it start trusting you before they call. It keeps working long after it's written.

options.text: Start a social media page and post daily product promotions
options.feedback: Daily promotions are ads you post yourself, on space you don't own. Buyers looking for answers will scroll right past them.

cards.title: Ask whether your marketing is rent or something you own.
body: Ads buy customers today. Useful content and a real community keep bringing them in, as long as you look after them.
**Try it today:** list the three questions customers ask you most. Could one answer, written down and shared, keep working for years?
